{{Top|leg|title=''Resol'nare'' rhyme|notoc=1}}
{{Conjecture|legends}}
{{Quote|Education and armor, self-defense, our tribe, our language, our leader—all help us survive. |[[Akaavi Spar]]|audio=ResolnareAkaaviSpar-TOR.flac|<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
[[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Youngling/Legends|children]] were taught a '''rhyme''' when they were young, in order to help them learn and remember the ''[[Resol'nare]]'', the six tenets of Mandalorian culture. In accordance with the ''Resol'nare'', the rhyme outlined the importance of learning the Mandalorian [[Language/Legends|language]] of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']], wearing [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]], being able to defend one's family and self, being loyal to the [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']], and raising one's children with those values.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>

The [[Gender/Legends|female]] Mandalorian [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]], [[Akaavi Spar]], recited the ''Resol'nare'' rhyme for [[Voidhound|the captain]] of a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Starship/Legends|ship]] she served on during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], while discussing the culture she came from and the six tenets that laid at its core.<ref name="TOR" />

|colspan="1"|''Ba'jur bal beskar'gam,<br />Ara'nov, aliit,<br />Mando'a bal Mand'alor—<br />An vencuyan mhi.<br />''||colspan="1"|Education and armor,<br />Self-defense, our tribe,<br />Our language and our leader—<br />All help us survive.<br />
|}

==Behind the scenes==
This rhyme was first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe via the second chapter epigraph of the [[2008]] novel ''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]'', by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]]. It was later quoted by the Mandalorian warrior Akaavi Spar, in the [[2012]] [[BioWare]]-made [[Star Wars video games|MMORPG]], ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''.
